target_customer: US government and defense buyers (Space Force, NRO type agencies) and commercial space operators
problem: Tracking and imaging objects in orbit, moving spacecraft and removing debris require maneuverable satellites that are costly and slow to build.
business_model: Government contracts and data sales for space domain awareness, spacecraft and mission software; hardware manufacturing
product_category: Maneuverable satellites and space domain awareness

founders.name: Ryan Westerdahl
founders.background_notes: YC page: about a decade in aerospace including 8.5 years at SpaceX.

founders.name: Tyler James Pierce
founders.background_notes: YC page: over a decade in aerospace and defense; employers not named.

founders.name: Patryk Wiatr
founders.background_notes: YC page: full stack software engineer with almost 10 years of experience.

competitors.name: HEO Robotics
competitors.what: Imaging of other satellites from payloads on commercial spacecraft for space domain awareness
competitors.traction_then: company founded 2016 per an aggregator; source is undated

competitors.name: Slingshot Aerospace
competitors.traction_then: founded 2016 or 2017 per aggregators; source is undated

technical_complexity.rationale: Building, launching and operating maneuverable satellites with propulsion and autonomy needs hardware, launch and regulatory approvals; a small team had to prove it with DROID.001, which launched in 2023 per Built In.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware heritage, government relationships and a US regulatory approval to sell space situational awareness services (August 2022) are hard to copy quickly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Traditional defense contractors still dominate military SDA programs per SpaceNews, but no source shows them copying or buying Turion; Turion instead acquired Tychee Research Group.

market_need_then: Growing orbital congestion and US defense interest in commercial space domain awareness and debris removal; later Space Force contract for debris capture technology (July 2024) confirms demand.

identity.logo: Original wordmark with an orbital motif tied to the debris removal focus, since refreshed
identity.visual_style: Rebrand by Buck and Wild beyond generic space defense look
identity.voice_and_tone: Taglines 'Accelerating humanity's galactic destiny' and 'Orbit with purpose'

branding.brand_signature: DROID satellite series and the Starforge asteroid mining ambition

rebrands.from: Original Turion identity with orbital wordmark
rebrands.to: New brand world and website by Buck and Wild
rebrands.why: To move beyond a generic space defense identity, per a Fast Company summary seen in search results; date not stated

branding.community_and_virality: Fast Company coverage of the rebrand; no merch or fan evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive name, a professional rebrand covered by Fast Company and a clear DROID product line, but the buyers are government and the brand is not a growth driver.

pivots.from: Debris removal and imaging of space objects
pivots.to: Broader orbital infrastructure: vehicles, mission software and payloads, with tactical space for defense
pivots.why: Company site now lists tactical space, mission software and space logistics; the reason and date are not stated

outcome_analysis: Turion has progressed from a three founder SpaceX alumni team with a seed round in 2021 to launching DROID.001 in 2023 and DROID.002 in 2025 per Built In, winning a Space Force debris capture contract in 2024, closing a Series A in late 2024 and a 75M dollar Series B in April 2026. Founder domain fit, hardware credibility and growing defense demand for space domain awareness explain the trajectory.
notes: Seed amount conflicts: the YC page and company description say a 6.2M dollar seed, Payload (November 2021) reports a 4.7M dollar close; recorded at 4.7M with the named investors. Series A amount is not disclosed; the Veteran Ventures piece says the company had raised nearly 20M in total; aggregators give 15M to 20M, unverified. An April 2025 Series A extension and Washington Harbour first investment appear in aggregators and a Washington Technology link, not recorded as a separate round. The two competitor sources are undated aggregator profiles of companies founded before 2021. Founded year is 2020 per the YC page; Built In says 2022.
